questions.question: The superintendent assured the Chief Justice that the technical team ___ the server migration by dawn.
questions.explanation: Main verb 'assured' Simple Past mein hai, isliye aage hone wale future action ke liye Future-in-the-Past ('would complete') aayega. 'Will complete' use karne se cross-clause tense harmony break hoti hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule TH-04: Jab principal verb past mein ho, toh future event ke liye 'would + V1' lagta hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L02

questions.question: The science professor demonstrated that copper ___ a superior conductor of electrical current.
questions.explanation: Copper ka electricity conduct karna physics ka ek immutable scientific law hai. Permanent scientific truths past reporting verb ('demonstrated') ke bawajood Simple Present ('is') mein hi rehte hain.
questions.ruleReference: Rule TH-05: Permanent scientific facts batane wale subordinate clauses Simple Present mein rehte hain.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L02

questions.question: The audit committee found that the contractor ___ substandard networking cables prior to inspection.
questions.explanation: Cables install karne ka kaam committee ke pata lagane se pehle hua tha (prior past event). Beete huye do events mein se pehle complete hone wale event ke liye Past Perfect ('had installed') aayega.
questions.ruleReference: Rule TH-03: Past reference point se pehle complete huye action ke liye Past Perfect ('had + V3') lagta hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L02

questions.subtopic: Purpose Clause with Past Main Verb
questions.question: The registrar instituted biometric authentication so that unauthorized entry ___ effectively prevented.
questions.explanation: Governing verb 'instituted' Simple Past (V2) mein hai. 'So that' wale purpose clauses mein past main verbs ke sath strictly past modal auxiliary 'might' ('might be prevented') lagta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule TH-08: Past Main Verb + 'so that' ke sath hamesha 'might + V1' lagta hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L02

questions.question: Find the incorrect part: The senior advocate stated (A) / during the hearing that (B) / the petitioner will file (C) / an amended appeal next week. (D)
questions.explanation: Past reporting verb 'stated' ke sath part (C) ka modal auxiliary 'will' tense harmony ke mutabiq backshift hokar 'would' ('would file') banna chahiye. 'Will' lagana modal discord error hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule TH-04: Past narrative frame mein 'will' ka backshift hokar 'would' banta hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L02

questions.subtopic: Open Sequence with Present Main Verb
questions.question: The administrative clerk affirms that the certified copies ___ ready for collection right now.
questions.explanation: Main verb 'affirms' Simple Present mein hai. Open Sequence Principle ke mutabiq yahan koi backshift nahi hoga. Time marker 'right now' current state show kar raha hai, isliye Present Be-verb 'are' lagega.
questions.ruleReference: Rule TH-01: Jab main clause verb present mein ho, toh subordinate clause apne time markers ke mutabiq tense leta hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L02

questions.question: The security guard noticed that an unidentified person ___ around the server room late last night.
questions.explanation: Main verb 'noticed' Simple Past (V2) hai. Loitering karne ka action past ke usi moment par notice karne ke sath-sath chal raha tha, isliye Past Continuous ('was loitering') aayega.
questions.ruleReference: Rule TH-02: Past narrative mein simultaneous progressive events ke liye Past Continuous lagta hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L02

questions.question: The history teacher noted that Maharana Pratap ___ valiantly in the Battle of Haldighati.
questions.explanation: Finished antiquity mein huye historical events ke liye Simple Past ('fought') lagta hai. Ye universal scientific truths nahi hain, isliye inhe Simple Present ('fights') mein nahi badla ja sakta.
questions.ruleReference: Rule TH-07: Historical events ke liye Simple Past (V2) use karein.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L02

questions.question: The veteran advocate prepared for high court appeals more meticulously than he ___ for subordinate court trials today.
questions.explanation: 'Than' wale subordinate clauses of comparison Rule of Past Harmony se exempt hote hain. Adverb 'today' current routine dikha raha hai, isliye Simple Present 'prepares' grammatically correct hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule TH-09: Comparison clauses logic aur sense ke mutabiq koi bhi tense le sakte hain.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L02

questions.question: The courtroom technician calibrated the audio system carefully lest the audio recording ___ distorted during the proceedings.
questions.explanation: Conjunction 'lest' ke sath strictly modal auxiliary 'should' aata hai ('lest the recording should become distorted').
questions.ruleReference: Rule TH-08: 'Lest' ke baad hamesha 'should + V1' lagta hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L02

questions.question: Spot the error: The judicial registrar worked (A) / through the weekend (B) / so that he may submit (C) / the inspection report on Monday. (D)
questions.explanation: Governing verb 'worked' Simple Past mein hai, isliye purpose clause modal strictly 'might' hona chahiye ('so that he might submit'). Part (C) mein galti se 'may' use kiya gaya hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule TH-08: Past Main Verb + 'so that' ke sath hamesha 'might + V1' lagta hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L02

questions.question: The teacher proved to the class that two and two ___ four.
questions.explanation: 'Two and two makes four' ek timeless mathematical axiom hai. Mathematical truths past tense backshifting se exempt rehte hain aur hamesha Simple Present ('makes') mein aate hain.
questions.ruleReference: Rule TH-05: Mathematical axioms hamesha Simple Present mein rehte hain.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L02

questions.question: Which of the following sentences adheres to correct tense harmony?

options.text: The magistrate said that he has visited the disputed site yesterday.
The magistrate said that he had visited the disputed site the day before.
The magistrate said that he will visit the disputed site tomorrow.
The magistrate says that he would visit the disputed site tomorrow.

questions.explanation: Option B poori tarah harmonious hai: past reporting verb 'said' ke sath pehle huye event ke liye Past Perfect 'had visited' aur time shift 'the day before' bilkul sahi hai. Option A mein past 'said' ke sath Present Perfect 'has visited' lagaya gaya hai jo galat hai. Option C mein 'will' ko 'would' mein backshift nahi kiya gaya. Option D mein present 'says' ke baad improper 'would' use kiya gaya hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule TH-03 & TH-04: Past reporting verb ke sath pehle ke event ke liye Past Perfect aur future event ke liye 'would' lagta hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L02

questions.question: The petitioner withdrew the special appeal because he ___ all statutory remedies available under state law.
questions.explanation: Statutory remedies exhaust karne ka kaam appeal withdraw karne se pehle hua tha. Past frame mein prior cause ke liye Past Perfect ('had exhausted') use hota hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule TH-03: Past effect se pehle huye cause ke liye Past Perfect ('had + V3') lagta hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L02

questions.question: The IT officer confirmed that the system administrator ___ the encrypted log files after the power backup ___.
questions.explanation: Teeno past events ka chronological order dekhein: (1) Sabse pehle power backup fail hua (earliest event ➔ 'had failed'). (2) Failure ke baad administrator ne files recover ki (intermediate event ➔ Simple Past 'recovered'). (3) Finally IT officer ne confirm kiya (main past verb 'confirmed'). Isliye option C ('recovered, had failed') grammatically aur chronologically bilkul perfect hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule TH-03: 'After' ke baad aane wala pehla action Past Perfect ('had failed') leta hai, aur baad wala resulting action Simple Past ('recovered') leta hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L02
